title: Multi-region backpressure extract / postmortem data pull
body:
Purpose:
Capture raw telemetry and derived metrics for the Nov 24-26 2026 multi-region backpressure incident to support the postmortem. This pull focuses on cross-region saturation, queue depth growth, throttle events and fallback routing behavior.

Scope/time-window:
- Incident window candidate: 2026-11-24 22:00 UTC to 2026-11-26 04:00 UTC (includes pre-onset 24h baseline and 24h after window).
- Regions included: us-west1, us-east1, europe-west1, apac-southeast1.
- Model families: rwd-llama-70b, rwd-llama-13b, rwd-retrieval-embed-v2.

Primary data sources and tables: (raw / derived)
- telemetry.api_requests (bigquery) -- one row per top-level request with model_id, region, route, start_ts, end_ts, tokens_out, client_tier.
- infra.gpu_metrics (prometheus/metrics-warehouse) -- 10s resolution: gpu_util_pct, gpu_mem_pct, host_cpu, nvlink_traffic, queue_depth_hint.
- serving.queue_events (kafka export) -- enqueue_ts, dequeue_ts, request_id, shard_id, queue_reason (cold-kv, contention).
- routing.events (bigquery) -- route decisions, fallback_model, region_fallback, capacity_tier.
- throttle.audit_log (s3 csv) -- timestamp, region, model_id, throttle_type (rate_limit, queue_shed), tokens_rejected

Recommended pulls (SQL / promql examples):
1) 1-minute aggregated GPU utilization by region + headroom estimate (BigQuery):

-- BigQuery SQL (example)
SELECT region, TIMESTAMP_TRUNC(TIMESTAMP_SECONDS(ts), MINUTE) AS minute,
  APPROX_QUANTILES(gpu_util_pct, 20)[OFFSET(10)] as p50_util,
  MAX(gpu_util_pct) as max_util,
  SUM(CASE WHEN gpu_util_pct > 92 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) as hotspot_10s_count
FROM `telemetry.infra.gpu_metrics`
WHERE ts BETWEEN UNIX_SECONDS(TIMESTAMP('2026-11-23')) AND UNIX_SECONDS(TIMESTAMP('2026-11-27'))
GROUP BY region, minute
ORDER BY minute;

2) PromQL snippet to get queue depth per host (10s resolution):
queue_pending_requests_total{job="serving",region=~"us-.*|europe.*"}

3) Join to find requests that experienced throttles and later eviction: (BigQuery join)
SELECT r.request_id, r.start_ts, t.throttle_ts, t.throttle_type, q.enqueue_ts, q.dequeue_ts, r.model_id, r.region
FROM `telemetry.api_requests` r
LEFT JOIN `telemetry.throttle_audit_log` t ON r.request_id = t.request_id
LEFT JOIN `telemetry.serving_queue_events` q ON r.request_id = q.request_id
WHERE r.start_ts BETWEEN TIMESTAMP('2026-11-24 00:00:00') AND TIMESTAMP('2026-11-26 23:59:59')
AND (t.throttle_type IS NOT NULL OR q.dequeue_ts IS NULL)
LIMIT 200000;

Column definitions (extracted for downstream teams):
- minute: minute bucket for aggregated metrics
- region: region tag (us-west1/us-east1/europe-west1/apac-southeast1)
- gpu_util_pct: per-GPU average utilization percent over sample window
- queue_depth_hint: heuristic queue length exposed by runtime (not precise QPS)
- tokens_out: number of tokens in response body (metric for cost/latency correlation)
- throttle_type: {rate_limit, queue_shed, model_fallback}
- fallback_model: model_id used when primary model was unavailable
- capacity_tier: {hosted,dedicated,private}

Sample rows (CSV-like excerpt):
minute,region,gpu_util_pct,queue_depth_hint,hotspot_count,tokens_out,throttle_type,fallback_model
2026-11-24T21:58Z,us-west1,91.2,12,3,45,rate_limit,rwd-llama-13b
2026-11-24T22:04Z,us-east1,94.7,28,9,120,queue_shed,
2026-11-25T00:12Z,europe-west1,65.3,2,0,32,,rwd-retrieval-embed-v2
2026-11-25T03:42Z,apac-southeast1,88.9,16,5,210,rate_limit,rwd-llama-13b

Key observations from raw pulls (first-pass):
- Us-east1 had a rapid queue depth spike starting ~2026-11-24 22:00 UTC coincident with a 15% increase in rwd-llama-70b traffic from a single customer (cust-867).
- Autoscaling did not add expected secondary shards for rwd-llama-70b in us-east1 due to a control-plane rate limiter (see routing.events snippets).
- Several hosts exhibited sustained GPU util > 92% for > 12 minutes which corresponds to increased KV cache misses (nvlink traffic uptick).
- Fallback routing moved traffic from us-east1 to us-west1 and europe-west1; us-west1 then saw localized hotspots and throttle events within 7 minutes of receiving fallback traffic.
- Throttle audit shows two distinct types: automated queue_shed (immediate rejection) and soft rate_limit (token-based delay). queue_shed events correlated with request_id patterns coming from the same IP ranges.

Timeline (consolidated):
- 2026-11-24 21:40 UTC: small uptick in rwd-llama-70b QPS (baseline +7%).
- 2026-11-24 21:58 UTC: localized hotspots in us-west1 detected (gpu_util > 90%).
- 2026-11-24 22:01 UTC: us-east1 queue depth climbs from 4 -> 28 in 3 minutes.
- 2026-11-24 22:03 UTC: control-plane scale API returned 429s for shard request (region rate limiter triggered).
- 2026-11-24 22:10 UTC: fallback routing starts moving rwd-llama-70b traffic across regions.
- 2026-11-24 22:17 UTC: us-west1 begins emitting throttle.audit (queue_shed) events.
- 2026-11-25 01:00 UTC: gradual recovery after customer traffic decreases; post-incident headroom re-established by 2026-11-25 03:00 UTC.

Root-cause hypotheses (to validate):
1) Control-plane region-level scaling rate limit prevented autoscaling from reacting quickly, creating longer queues and cascading fallbacks.
2) A single large customer (cust-867) increased model concurrency with long responses, causing sustained high GPU utilization; cache miss amplification made per-request cost worse.
3) Fallback logic lacks smoothing — moving a large share of traffic instantly into neighboring regions created secondary hotspots rather than gradual spillover.

Cross-checks / data validation steps:
- Correlate throttle.audit entries with routing.events to confirm whether throttles were local or caused by cross-region spill.
- Check autoscaler logs for 429 responses / throttled API calls during the window. (link: GCP-ops/scale-api-logs)
- Review kv-cache hit rates per host around hotspot windows (table: infra.kv_cache_stats).
- Validate that observed queue_depth_hint aligns with serving.queue_events enqueue/dequeue counts.

Immediate action items (short-term mitigations):
- [P0] Temporarily increase control-plane scale rate limit for rwd-llama-70b in us-east1 while we investigate (owner: Marco Ruiz).
- [P1] Add smoothing window (5–10 minute ramp) to fallback routing policy to avoid instantaneous full spill. (owner: Jingwei Chen).
- [P1] Create monitoring alert for sustained GPU_util_pct > 90% across >3 hosts in same AZ. (owner: SRE team).
- [P2] Flag cust-867 for traffic shaping during peak hours and coordinate with Customer Success for plan. (owner: Solutions Eng).

Longer-term changes to evaluate:
- Region-aware autoscaler backoff reduction when control-plane returns a 429 (so we retry faster with exponential jitter).
- Per-customer concurrency caps for chosen model families to limit single-tenant shock.
- Improve kv-cache priming and prefetch heuristics for long-running response generators.

Notes for downstream teams:
- The attached SQL pulls are heavy (scan across telemetry tables). Use sampled date ranges for iterative work and persist aggregated intermediate tables for the postmortem notebook.
- Ensure privacy: customer ids in the pulls are pseudonymized for external sharing.

Appendix: useful queries + storage location
- Aggregated output (minute-level) exported to gs://redwood-postmortem/multi-region-backpressure/aggregates/2026-11-27/
- Raw queue events export (parquet) in s3://telemetry-exports/multi-region-backpressure/2026-11-27/

Next steps / owners:
- Data team: finalize cleaned aggregates and share notebook (due 2026-12-02). (owner: Aisha Patel)
- Infra eng: implement fallback smoothing experiment (due 2026-12-09). (owner: Jingwei Chen)
- SRE: create/add alert and run tabletop to validate escalation runbook. (due 2026-12-03).

-- End of pull sheet --
